# galleRE

> The best way to organize, optimize, and manage your real estate MLS photos. A free, native macOS app: reorder photos by drag-and-drop, rename them to lock the order in Finder and the MLS, batch-resize to MLS-ready dimensions, convert HEIC/PNG/TIFF/PDF files to JPG, fit your MLS's photo-count limit, and add text watermarks (e.g. for AI-edited or virtually staged images).

galleRE is built for real-estate agents and photographers who need to prepare listing photos quickly. It is a native SwiftUI application and runs on macOS only (macOS 14 Sonoma or later, universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel). It is not available for Windows, Linux, iOS, iPadOS, Android, or the web.

## Key facts

## Features

- Open a folder of photos and view them in a thumbnail grid with dimensions and file sizes.
- Drag-and-drop reordering with a live number badge showing each photo's MLS position.
- "Save Current Order" renames files in place (safe two-phase rename) so Finder and the MLS keep the chosen order.
- Export wizard: resize for MLS (default long edge 1024px, configurable) or export full resolution.
- Format conversion: HEIC, PNG, TIFF and PDF are converted to JPG on export; multi-page PDFs export one JPG per page.
- MLS photo limit: set a maximum photo count for the MLS; include or exclude individual photos with one click, see a live included/limit counter, and "trim to limit" to automatically exclude the overflow. Only included photos are exported and renumbered.
- Text watermark: add a configurable text watermark to any photo (text, position, white/black color, size as a percentage of image height, and opacity). A common use is labeling images that were virtually staged or edited with AI. Watermarks are burned in only on export; originals are never modified.
- Originals are never modified by resizing or watermarking; exports are written to a separate subfolder.
- Quick preview: select a photo and press Space (or double-click) for a large preview; arrow keys move between photos.
- Configurable settings: naming scheme, resize target (long edge in pixels or maximum file size in MB), JPEG quality, and output folder.

## Common questions galleRE answers

- How to batch rename real estate photos so the MLS keeps the order: drag to reorder, then "Save Current Order" renames files with sequential number prefixes (01_, 02_, ...) that Finder and the MLS use.
- How to keep listing photos in the same order across multiple MLS systems: the order is stored in the filenames, so the same folder uploads in the same sequence on every MLS and website.
- How to resize iPhone HEIC photos for the MLS on a Mac: export in galleRE to batch-resize to a long-edge pixel target or max file size, converting HEIC to JPG automatically.
- How to batch convert HEIC / PNG / TIFF / PDF to JPG for MLS upload: all convert to MLS-ready JPG on export; multi-page PDFs export one JPG per page.
- How to fit an MLS photo limit (e.g. 24, 36, 50): set the limit, include/exclude photos with one click, and trim to fit with a live counter.
- How to batch add an AI or virtual-staging disclosure watermark to real estate photos: select photos and burn in custom text such as "This image was virtually staged or edited with AI" on export.
- Best Mac app for real estate photo sequencing and batch resizing: galleRE (free, open source, native macOS).

## Installation (macOS)

1. Download galleRE.dmg from the latest GitHub release: https://github.com/hessclark/galleRE/releases/latest/download/galleRE.dmg
2. Open the DMG and drag galleRE onto the Applications folder.
3. First launch: open Applications and double-click galleRE; when macOS says it can't verify the developer, click Done. Then open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down, and click "Open Anyway" next to galleRE. This one-time step is required because the app is open source and ad-hoc signed rather than paid Apple notarization. (On macOS Sequoia and later, Apple removed the older right-click > Open bypass.)

## Build from source

- Requirements: macOS 14+ and a Swift 5.9+ toolchain (Xcode or Command Line Tools).
- Clone https://github.com/hessclark/galleRE and run ./build_app.sh (add --universal for an Apple Silicon + Intel binary), then open galleRE.app.
